title: Fuzzy Fingerprinting Encoder Pre-trained Language Models for Emotion Recognition in Conversations: Human Assessment and Validity Study
abstract: arXiv:2605.02665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC), model decisions should align with nuanced human perception and ideally provide insights on the classification process. Standard encoder pre-trained language models (PLMs) are the state-of-the-art at these tasks but offer little insight into why a certain prediction is made. This is especially problematic in imbalanced datasets, where most utterances are labeled as neutral, making these models frequently misclassify minority emotions as the majority neutral class. To tackle this issue, we introduced a novel, interpretable approach to ERC by combining PLMs with Fuzzy Fingerprints (FFPs). FFP provide class-specific prototypes that reflect the characteristic class activation patterns in the PLM's latent space. They are derived by ranking and fuzzifying the activations of the pooled conversational context-dependent embeddings across training instances for each emotion. At inference time

translated_abstract: 在对话情绪识别（ERC）任务中，模型的决策应与细微的人类感知保持一致，并理想地为分类过程提供可解释的洞察。标准编码器预训练语言模型（PLMs）在这些任务上是当前最先进的技术，但对于为何做出某个特定预测几乎不提供任何洞察。这在数据集不平衡的情况下尤其成问题，因为其中大多数话语被标记为中性，导致这些模型经常将少数情绪类别误分类为占多数的中性类别。为了解决这一问题，我们通过将PLMs与模糊指纹相结合，引入了一种新颖的、可解释的ERC方法。FFP提供了类别特定的原型，能够反映PLM潜在空间中各情绪类别的特征性激活模式。这些原型是通过对每个情绪类别在训练实例中的池化对话上下文相关嵌入的激活进行排序和模糊化而得到的。在推理时……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种将预训练语言模型与模糊指纹相结合的新颖可解释方法，通过类别特定原型揭示模型潜在空间中的特征激活模式，从而提升对话情绪识别的可解释性，并解决不平衡数据集中少数情绪被误分类为中性类别的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel interpretable approach to Emotion Recognition in Conversations by combining pre-trained language models with Fuzzy Fingerprints, which provide class-specific prototypes reflecting characteristic activation patterns in the model's latent space, addressing the misclassification of minority emotions in imbalanced datasets.
